column9: Pairs with 就: 動不動就哭, 動不動就感冒. The speaker is complaining that something happens too easily, so it is for bad habits, not good ones.

column3: A grammar term from Chinese lessons, like 名词 (noun) and 形容词 (adjective). 及物动词 is a transitive verb and 助动词 an auxiliary such as 能 or 会.
column6: Chī shì dòngcí, bù shì míngcí.
column7: Eat is a verb, not a noun.
column9: A grammar term from Chinese lessons, like 名詞 (noun) and 形容詞 (adjective). 及物動詞 is a transitive verb and 助動詞 an auxiliary such as 能 or 會.

column3: Setting out on a trip, with the place after 去: 动身去北京. It is the moment of starting a journey, not leaving a room or a party; that is 离开.
column6: Wǒmen míngtiān yīzǎo jiù dòngshēn.
column7: We set off first thing tomorrow morning.
column9: Setting out on a trip, with the place after 去: 動身去北京. It is the moment of starting a journey, not leaving a room or a party; that is 離開.

column3: A heavy word of politics and history (阶级斗争) and of inner conflict (思想斗争). A fistfight or a quarrel is 打架 or 吵架, not 斗争.
column4: 他心里正在进行思想斗争。
column5: 他心裡正在進行思想鬥爭。
column6: Tā xīnlǐ zhèngzài jìnxíng sīxiǎng dòuzhēng.
column7: He is having an inner struggle.
column9: A heavy word of politics and history (階級鬥爭) and of inner conflict (思想鬥爭). A fistfight or a quarrel is 打架 or 吵架, not 鬥爭.

column3: For real gambling and friendly bets alike: 赌钱, 打赌 (make a bet), 赌博 (gambling as an activity). 我跟你赌… is the way to say 'I bet you…'.
column6: Wǒ gǎn gēn nǐ dǔ tā bù huì lái.
column7: I bet you he won't come.
column9: For real gambling and friendly bets alike: 賭錢, 打賭 (make a bet), 賭博 (gambling as an activity). 我跟你賭… is the way to say 'I bet you…'.

column3: For carrying something level in front of you: a bowl, a tray, a cup of tea: 端菜, 端茶. Compare 拿 (take) and 提 (carry hanging). The 'end' sense is in 顶端 and 末端.
column6: Fúwùshēng bǎ tāng duān dào zhuō shàng.
column7: The waiter carried the soup to the table.
column9: For carrying something level in front of you: a bowl, a tray, a cup of tea: 端菜, 端茶. Compare 拿 (take) and 提 (carry hanging). The 'end' sense is in 頂端 and 末端.

column3: Used for getting through a hardship: 渡过难关, 渡过危机. A stretch of time is 度过 (度过童年, 度过假期), and 渡过 is also literally crossing water.
column4: 我们一起渡过了很多困难。
column5: 我們一起渡過了很多困難。
column6: Wǒmen yīqǐ dùguò le hěn duō kùnnán.
column7: We got through many difficulties together.
column9: Used for getting through a hardship: 渡過難關, 渡過危機. A stretch of time is 度過 (度過童年, 度過假期), and 渡過 is also literally crossing water.

column3: Used for the far side of a river, lake or sea. In Taiwanese news it is also a way of saying mainland China, across the Strait; mainland sources say 大陆 for the same place.
column6: Hé de duì'àn yǒu yī zuò xiǎo shān.
column7: There is a small hill on the other side of the river.
column9: Used for the far side of a river, lake or sea. In Taiwanese news it is also a way of saying mainland China, across the Strait; mainland sources say 大陸 for the same place.

column3: It answers a specific problem and goes with verbs like 想, 研究, 提出 and 制定: 针对这个问题提出对策. Common in news, meetings and reports.
column6: Wǒmen bìxū xiǎng chū duìcè.
column7: We must come up with a countermeasure.
column9: It answers a specific problem and goes with verbs like 想, 研究, 提出 and 制定: 針對這個問題提出對策. Common in news, meetings and reports.

column3: Two sides or forces set against each other: 对抗赛 is a match between two teams, and 对抗病毒 or 与……对抗 is standing against a threat. It is more neutral than 反抗, which means rebelling against authority.
column4: 两个队伍在比赛中互相对抗。
column5: 兩個隊伍在比賽中互相對抗。
column6: Liǎng ge duìwǔ zài bǐsài zhōng hùxiāng duìkàng.
column7: The two teams compete against each other in the match.
column9: Two sides or forces set against each other: 對抗賽 is a match between two teams, and 對抗病毒 or 與……對抗 is standing against a threat. It is more neutral than 反抗, which means rebelling against authority.

column3: Goes with a direction or place: 蹲下, 蹲在门口. People and animals both do it. It can also mean to stay put somewhere dull, as in 蹲在家里 (stuck at home), and 蹲监狱 is to do time.
column4: 他蹲下来帮孩子系鞋带。
column5: 他蹲下來幫孩子繫鞋帶。
column6: Tā dūn xiàlái bāng háizi jì xiédài.
column7: He squatted down to tie the child's shoelaces.
column9: Goes with a direction or place: 蹲下, 蹲在門口. People and animals both do it. It can also mean to stay put somewhere dull, as in 蹲在家裡 (stuck at home), and 蹲監獄 is to do time.

column3: Mostly found in compounds: 夺冠 (win the title), 夺取, 抢夺 and 剥夺. For a prize or victory it is 夺得 or 夺取; the grabbing sense is a bit forceful.
column4: 他夺得了比赛的第一名。
column5: 他奪得了比賽的第一名。
column6: Tā duó dé le bǐsài de dì-yī míng.
column7: He won first place in the competition.
column9: Mostly found in compounds: 奪冠 (win the title), 奪取, 搶奪 and 剝奪. For a prize or victory it is 奪得 or 奪取; the grabbing sense is a bit forceful.

column3: Put before a verb, it is a guess that leans toward yes: 他多半不会来. With 的 and a noun it means the greater part: 多半的人, though 大多数 is more common there.
column4: 今天这么晚，他多半不会来了。
column5: 今天這麼晚，他多半不會來了。
column6: Jīntiān zhème wǎn, tā duōbàn bù huì lái le.
column7: It is so late; he most likely won't come.
column9: Put before a verb, it is a guess that leans toward yes: 他多半不會來. With 的 and a noun it means the greater part: 多半的人, though 大多數 is more common there.

column3: Mostly in polite set phrases, where doubling adds warmth: 多多指教, 多多关照, 多多保重. It is not used freely like 很多; 多多益善 is the saying for the more the better.
column6: Qǐng dàjiā duōduō zhǐjiào.
column7: Please give us your guidance.
column9: Mostly in polite set phrases, where doubling adds warmth: 多多指教, 多多關照, 多多保重. It is not used freely like 很多; 多多益善 is the saying for the more the better.

column3: An ordinary thanks, a little warmer than 谢谢. It can stand alone (多谢!) or take a person or a favor: 多谢你, 多谢帮忙.
column6: Duōxiè nǐ bāng wǒ zhège máng.
column7: Many thanks for helping me.
column9: An ordinary thanks, a little warmer than 謝謝. It can stand alone (多謝!) or take a person or a favor: 多謝你, 多謝幫忙.

column3: Counted with 只: 一只鹅. Also in 天鹅 (swan) and 鹅卵石, a smooth rounded pebble, named for its goose-egg shape.
column6: Hébiān yǒu jǐ zhī bái é.
column7: There are some white geese by the river.
column9: Counted with 隻: 一隻鵝. Also in 天鵝 (swan) and 鵝卵石, a smooth rounded pebble, named for its goose-egg shape.

column3: A written, stronger word than 坏, for conditions and conduct: 天气恶劣, 环境恶劣, 态度恶劣, 影响恶劣. It describes things and behavior more than it names a person.
column4: 因为天气恶劣，航班取消了。
column5: 因為天氣惡劣，航班取消了。
column6: Yīnwèi tiānqì èliè, hángbān qǔxiāo le.
column7: The flight was canceled because of the foul weather.
column9: A written, stronger word than 壞, for conditions and conduct: 天氣惡劣, 環境惡劣, 態度惡劣, 影響惡劣. It describes things and behavior more than it names a person.

column3: Closes a sentence, usually after 只是, 不过 or 仅仅, to play the matter down: 不过是小事而已. Neutral, in speech and writing; 罢了 does the same job.
column6: Wǒ zhǐshì kāi wánxiào éryǐ.
column7: I was only joking.
column9: Closes a sentence, usually after 只是, 不過 or 僅僅, to play the matter down: 不過是小事而已. Neutral, in speech and writing; 罷了 does the same job.

column3: Usually 得 comes first with the cause: 冷得发抖, 吓得发抖, 气得发抖. 发 before a state often means to come out in it, as in 发烧 and 发呆.
column6: Tā lěng de quánshēn fādǒu.
column7: He is shivering all over from the cold.
column9: Usually 得 comes first with the cause: 冷得發抖, 嚇得發抖, 氣得發抖. 發 before a state often means to come out in it, as in 發燒 and 發呆.

column3: A measure word that needs 一 or another number and tells you an action took time or effort: 一番话, 费了一番功夫, 三番五次. After 翻 it counts doublings: 翻一番 is to double.
column4: 他花了一番功夫才找到这里。
column5: 他花了一番功夫才找到這裡。
column6: Tā huā le yī fān gōngfu cái zhǎodào zhèlǐ.
column7: It took him a good deal of effort to find this place.
column9: A measure word that needs 一 or another number and tells you an action took time or effort: 一番話, 費了一番功夫, 三番五次. After 翻 it counts doublings: 翻一番 is to double.

column3: A verb plus object, so it splits: 犯了错, 犯错误. The mistake is one of judgment or conduct; a slip in spelling or calculation is 写错 or 算错. 犯 starts many such words: 犯法, 犯罪, 犯规.
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yǒu kěnéng fàncuò.
column7: Anyone can make a mistake.
column9: A verb plus object, so it splits: 犯了錯, 犯錯誤. The mistake is one of judgment or conduct; a slip in spelling or calculation is 寫錯 or 算錯. 犯 starts many such words: 犯法, 犯罪, 犯規.

column3: A verb plus object, so 了 goes in the middle: 犯了法. Plain and spoken: 这样做犯法. 违法 means the same and is the more formal, written choice.
column6: Jiǔ hòu kāichē shì fànfǎ de.
column7: Driving after drinking breaks the law.
column9: A verb plus object, so 了 goes in the middle: 犯了法. Plain and spoken: 這樣做犯法. 違法 means the same and is the more formal, written choice.

column3: The standard sports word, opposite 进攻: 防守反击 is a counterattack, 防守严密 is tight defense. In war and security it is about holding a position: 防守边境.
column4: 我们的队伍防守得很好。
column5: 我們的隊伍防守得很好。
column6: Wǒmen de duìwǔ fángshǒu de hěn hǎo.
column7: Our team defends very well.
column9: The standard sports word, opposite 進攻: 防守反擊 is a counterattack, 防守嚴密 is tight defense. In war and security it is about holding a position: 防守邊境.

column3: Literal: 别放手 means do not let go of the rope. Figurative: 放手让孩子做 gives someone full freedom to act, and 放手一搏 is going all out.
column4: 你应该放手让孩子自己试试。
column5: 你應該放手讓孩子自己試試。
column6: Nǐ yīnggāi fàngshǒu ràng háizi zìjǐ shìshi.
column7: You should let go and let the child try for himself.
column9: Literal: 別放手 means do not let go of the rope. Figurative: 放手讓孩子做 gives someone full freedom to act, and 放手一搏 is going all out.

column3: Fighting back against someone with power over you: 反抗压迫, 反抗父母. Stronger than 反对, which can be only disagreeing; 反抗 is acting against it.
column4: 青少年常常反抗父母的管教。
column5: 青少年常常反抗父母的管教。
column6: Qīngshàonián chángcháng fǎnkàng fùmǔ de guǎnjiào.
column7: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' discipline.
column9: Fighting back against someone with power over you: 反抗壓迫, 反抗父母. Stronger than 反對, which can be only disagreeing; 反抗 is acting against it.

column3: A written word for schedules, jobs, traffic and places: 工作繁忙, 繁忙的街道, 繁忙时段. About yourself you would say 我很忙 instead.
column4: 这条街上的交通非常繁忙。
column5: 這條街上的交通非常繁忙。
column6: Zhè tiáo jiē shàng de jiāotōng fēicháng fánmáng.
column7: The traffic on this street is very busy.
column9: A written word for schedules, jobs, traffic and places: 工作繁忙, 繁忙的街道, 繁忙時段. About yourself you would say 我很忙 instead.

column3: Opposite 正面. The back of a sheet, card or coin, and the negative side of a matter: 反面教材 is a bad example used for teaching, and 反面人物 is the villain.
column4: 请在纸的反面写你的名字。
column5: 請在紙的反面寫你的名字。
column6: Qǐng zài zhǐ de fǎnmiàn xiě nǐ de míngzi.
column7: Please write your name on the back of the paper.
column9: Opposite 正面. The back of a sheet, card or coin, and the negative side of a matter: 反面教材 is a bad example used for teaching, and 反面人物 is the villain.

column3: The plain word for someone held or sentenced for a crime. 罪犯 is the more formal term in news and law, and 嫌疑犯 is a suspect not yet convicted.
column6: Jǐngchá zhuādào le nàge fànrén.
column7: The police caught that criminal.
column9: The plain word for someone held or sentenced for a crime. 罪犯 is the more formal term in news and law, and 嫌疑犯 is a suspect not yet convicted.

column3: Both a verb, as in the example, and a noun: 反问句 is a rhetorical question such as 难道你不知道吗？, which asks to make a point rather than to get an answer.
column4: 他没回答，反问了我一个问题。
column5: 他沒回答，反問了我一個問題。
column6: Tā méi huídá, fǎnwèn le wǒ yī ge wèntí.
column7: He did not answer but asked me a question back.
column9: Both a verb, as in the example, and a noun: 反問句 is a rhetorical question such as 難道你不知道嗎？, which asks to make a point rather than to get an answer.

column3: A biology word for living things multiplying: 繁殖后代, 繁殖季节, 细菌繁殖. For people having children, say 生孩子 or the formal 生育.
column4: 春天是很多动物繁殖的季节。
column5: 春天是很多動物繁殖的季節。
column6: Chūntiān shì hěn duō dòngwù fánzhí de jìjié.
column7: Spring is the breeding season for many animals.
column9: A biology word for living things multiplying: 繁殖後代, 繁殖季節, 細菌繁殖. For people having children, say 生孩子 or the formal 生育.

column3: Works as a verb (他犯罪了) and as a noun (犯罪率, 打击犯罪). It is the general term; one particular offense is 罪行, and the offender is 罪犯.
column4: 警察正在调查这起犯罪事件。
column5: 警察正在調查這起犯罪事件。
column6: Jǐngchá zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ fànzuì shìjiàn.
column7: The police are investigating this criminal case.
column9: Works as a verb (他犯罪了) and as a noun (犯罪率, 打擊犯罪). It is the general term; one particular offense is 罪行, and the offender is 罪犯.

column3: The object is an event or campaign: 发起活动, 发起募捐, 发起挑战, 发起进攻. 发起人 is the person who starts it and gets others to join.
column4: 几位同学发起了募款活动。
column5: 幾位同學發起了募款活動。
column6: Jǐ wèi tóngxué fāqǐ le mùkuǎn huódòng.
column7: A few classmates started a fund-raising event.
column9: The object is an event or campaign: 發起活動, 發起募捐, 發起挑戰, 發起進攻. 發起人 is the person who starts it and gets others to join.

column3: Goes with 换, 设计 and 新: 换发型, 新发型. The haircut itself is 理发 or 剪头发; 发型 is the finished look.
column6: Nǐ de xīn fàxíng hěn hǎokàn.
column7: Your new hairstyle looks very nice.
column9: Goes with 換, 設計 and 新: 換髮型, 新髮型. The haircut itself is 理髮 or 剪頭髮; 髮型 is the finished look.

column3: Said of a body part or wound that has turned red and sore: 喉咙发炎了, 伤口发炎. 炎 ends many illness words, like 肺炎 and 胃炎.
column6: Wǒ de hóulóng fāyán le, hěn tòng.
column7: My throat is inflamed and hurts a lot.
column9: Said of a body part or wound that has turned red and sore: 喉嚨發炎了, 傷口發炎. 炎 ends many illness words, like 肺炎 and 胃炎.

column3: Takes good, abstract things worth keeping and growing: 发扬传统, 发扬精神, 发扬风格, and the set phrase 发扬光大. Not used for concrete things or bad habits.
column4: 我们应该发扬这种好传统。
column5: 我們應該發揚這種好傳統。
column6: Wǒmen yīnggāi fāyáng zhè zhǒng hǎo chuántǒng.
column7: We should carry forward this good tradition.
column9: Takes good, abstract things worth keeping and growing: 發揚傳統, 發揚精神, 發揚風格, and the set phrase 發揚光大. Not used for concrete things or bad habits.

column3: How you say a word: 发音标准, 发音不准, 练习发音. For the reading a dictionary lists for a character or word, 读音 is the usual word.
column6: Tā de Zhōngwén fāyīn hěn biāozhǔn.
column7: His Chinese pronunciation is very standard.
column9: How you say a word: 發音標準, 發音不准, 練習發音. For the reading a dictionary lists for a character or word, 讀音 is the usual word.

column3: A chatty word for a way out of a problem: 想法子, 没法子 (nothing can be done), 有什么法子. 办法 is the all-purpose word; 法子 sounds more like casual talk.
column4: 这个问题我想不出什么法子。
column5: 這個問題我想不出什麼法子。
column6: Zhège wèntí wǒ xiǎng bù chū shénme fǎzi.
column7: I can't think of any way to deal with this problem.
column9: A chatty word for a way out of a problem: 想法子, 沒法子 (nothing can be done), 有什麼法子. 辦法 is the all-purpose word; 法子 sounds more like casual talk.

column3: Shows up in illness and health words: 肺炎, 肺癌, 肺部, 肺活量. The expression 肺腑之言 means words from the heart.
column4: 他的肺不太好，一跑步就喘。
column5: 他的肺不太好，一跑步就喘。
column6: Tā de fèi bù tài hǎo, yī pǎobù jiù chuǎn.
column7: His lungs aren't great; he gets out of breath whenever he runs.
column9: Shows up in illness and health words: 肺炎, 肺癌, 肺部, 肺活量. The expression 肺腑之言 means words from the heart.

column3: A formal word that goes before a noun, in news and law: 非法入境, 非法经营, 非法集会. Its opposite is 合法. 非 works as non- elsewhere too: 非正式.
column4: 他因为非法入境被抓了。
column5: 他因為非法入境被抓了。
column6: Tā yīnwèi fēifǎ rùjìng bèi zhuā le.
column7: He was arrested for entering illegally.
column9: A formal word that goes before a noun, in news and law: 非法入境, 非法經營, 非法集會. Its opposite is 合法. 非 works as non- elsewhere too: 非正式.

column3: A scolding: 别说废话 and 废话少说 (get to the point). As a one-word retort, 废话！ means duh or no kidding, and is rude except among close friends.
column6: Bié shuō fèihuà, kuài diǎn zuòshì!
column7: Stop the nonsense and get on with it!
column9: A scolding: 別說廢話 and 廢話少說 (get to the point). As a one-word retort, 廢話！ means duh or no kidding, and is rude except among close friends.

column3: A clinical word from health writing: 肥胖症, 肥胖率, 预防肥胖. In daily talk people say 胖; 肥 on its own is blunt for a person and is for meat (肥肉), animals or loose clothes.
column4: 肥胖会增加得病的机会。
column5: 肥胖會增加得病的機會。
column6: Féipàng huì zēngjiā dé bìng de jīhuì.
column7: Obesity raises the chance of falling ill.
column9: A clinical word from health writing: 肥胖症, 肥胖率, 預防肥胖. In daily talk people say 胖; 肥 on its own is blunt for a person and is for meat (肥肉), animals or loose clothes.

column3: An environmental word for gas from engines and factories: 汽车废气, 工业废气, 排放废气. 废 before a noun marks waste: 废水, 废纸, 废电池.
column4: 汽车的废气会造成空气污染。
column5: 汽車的廢氣會造成空氣污染。
column6: Qìchē de fèiqì huì zàochéng kōngqì wūrǎn.
column7: Car exhaust causes air pollution.
column9: An environmental word for gas from engines and factories: 汽車廢氣, 工業廢氣, 排放廢氣. 廢 before a noun marks waste: 廢水, 廢紙, 廢電池.

column3: An environmental term for water left over from factories, farms or processes: 工业废水, 处理废水, 排放废水. 污水 is the wider word for any dirty or sewage water.
column4: 工厂不能随便排放废水。
column5: 工廠不能隨便排放廢水。
column6: Gōngchǎng bù néng suíbiàn páifàng fèishuǐ.
column7: Factories may not discharge waste water as they like.
column9: An environmental term for water left over from factories, farms or processes: 工業廢水, 處理廢水, 排放廢水. 污水 is the wider word for any dirty or sewage water.

column3: Waste from industry, hospitals or a process: 有害废物, 医疗废物, 废物利用. Household trash is 垃圾. Said of a person it is a harsh insult.
column4: 这些废物应该分类处理。
column5: 這些廢物應該分類處理。
column6: Zhèxiē fèiwù yīnggāi fēnlèi chǔlǐ.
column7: This waste should be sorted and handled.
column9: Waste from industry, hospitals or a process: 有害廢物, 醫療廢物, 廢物利用. Household trash is 垃圾. Said of a person it is a harsh insult.

column3: Names what is due to someone: 你的份儿, 有你一份儿, 没你的份儿 (nothing for you). A written or neutral choice is 份 alone, also a measure word: 一份饭.
column4: 这是你的份儿，快拿去吧。
column5: 這是你的份兒，快拿去吧。
column6: Zhè shì nǐ de fènr, kuài ná qù ba.
column7: This is your share; take it.
column9: Names what is due to someone: 你的份兒, 有你一份兒, 沒你的份兒 (nothing for you). A written or neutral choice is 份 alone, also a measure word: 一份飯.

column3: Counted with 支 or 根: 一支粉笔; 粉笔灰 is chalk dust and 粉笔字 is writing in chalk. 笔 ends other writing tools too: 铅笔, 钢笔, 毛笔.
column4: 老师用粉笔在黑板上写字。
column5: 老師用粉筆在黑板上寫字。
column6: Lǎoshī yòng fěnbǐ zài hēibǎn shàng xiě zì.
column7: The teacher writes on the blackboard with chalk.
column9: Counted with 支 or 根: 一支粉筆; 粉筆灰 is chalk dust and 粉筆字 is writing in chalk. 筆 ends other writing tools too: 鉛筆, 鋼筆, 毛筆.

column3: Instructions from someone senior: 老板吩咐我, 照你的吩咐. A server or host asks 有什幺吩咐 to offer service. Not for giving orders to an equal.
column4: 老板吩咐我今天把报告做完。
column5: 老闆吩咐我今天把報告做完。
column6: Lǎobǎn fēnfu wǒ jīntiān bǎ bàogào zuò wán.
column7: The boss told me to finish the report today.
column9: Instructions from someone senior: 老板吩咐我, 照你的吩咐. A server or host asks 有什么吩咐 to offer service. Not for giving orders to an equal.

column3: A written word for whenever a time comes round, usually as 每逢: 每逢周末, 逢年过节, 逢人便说. It also means meeting by chance in 相逢 and 重逢 (meeting again).
column4: 每逢星期六，我们都去爷爷家吃饭。
column5: 每逢星期六，我們都去爺爺家吃飯。
column6: Měi féng xīngqīliù, wǒmen dōu qù yéye jiā chī fàn.
column7: Every Saturday we go to Grandpa's house for dinner.
column9: A written word for whenever a time comes round, usually as 每逢: 每逢週末, 逢年過節, 逢人便說. It also means meeting by chance in 相逢 and 重逢 (meeting again).

column3: 缝纫机 is a sewing machine; the verb takes what is sewn: 缝衣服, 缝扣子, 缝伤口 (stitch up a wound). As a noun it means a crack or seam, in 裂缝 and 缝隙.
column6: Māma zài gěi wǒ féng yīfu.
column7: Mom is sewing clothes for me.
column9: 縫紉機 is a sewing machine; the verb takes what is sewn: 縫衣服, 縫釦子, 縫傷口 (stitch up a wound). As a noun it means a crack or seam, in 裂縫 and 縫隙.

column3: A verb and a noun. The target is a person, society or situation: 讽刺别人, 讽刺漫画; 真讽刺 is how ironic. The jab is indirect, unlike 嘲笑, which is plain laughing at someone.
column4: 这部电影讽刺了社会的问题。
column5: 這部電影諷刺了社會的問題。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng fěngcì le shèhuì de wèntí.
column7: This film satirizes the problems of society.
column9: A verb and a noun. The target is a person, society or situation: 諷刺別人, 諷刺漫畫; 真諷刺 is how ironic. The jab is indirect, unlike 嘲笑, which is plain laughing at someone.

column3: Two uses: history, as in 封建社会 and 封建王朝, and in speech a mild criticism of old-fashioned, rigid thinking: 太封建了, 封建思想.
column6: Zhè zhǒng xiǎngfǎ tài fēngjiàn le.
column7: This way of thinking is too old-fashioned.
column9: Two uses: history, as in 封建社會 and 封建王朝, and in speech a mild criticism of old-fashioned, rigid thinking: 太封建了, 封建思想.

column3: Counted by the jar or spoon: 一罐蜂蜜, 一勺蜂蜜. Common in drinks and sweets: 蜂蜜水, 蜂蜜柚子茶, 蜂蜜蛋糕. The characters flipped, 蜜蜂, is the honeybee.
column4: 我喜欢在茶里放一点蜂蜜。
column5: 我喜歡在茶裡放一點蜂蜜。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan zài chá lǐ fàng yīdiǎn fēngmì.
column7: I like to put a little honey in my tea.
column9: Counted by the jar or spoon: 一罐蜂蜜, 一勺蜂蜜. Common in drinks and sweets: 蜂蜜水, 蜂蜜柚子茶, 蜂蜜蛋糕. The characters flipped, 蜜蜂, is the honeybee.

column3: Both a verb and a noun, about who does which part: 分工合作, 明确分工, 社会分工 (division of labor in society).
column4: 我们要分工合作，才能快点完成。
column5: 我們要分工合作，才能快點完成。
column6: Wǒmen yào fēngōng hézuò, cái néng kuài diǎn wánchéng.
column7: We must divide up the work and cooperate to finish quickly.
column9: Both a verb and a noun, about who does which part: 分工合作, 明確分工, 社會分工 (division of labor in society).

column3: The shared mood or habits of a school, workplace or era, good or bad: 社会风气, 学习风气, 不良风气, 败坏风气. It is not the weather and not one person's habit.
column4: 这个学校有很好的学习风气。
column5: 這個學校有很好的學習風氣。
column6: Zhège xuéxiào yǒu hěn hǎo de xuéxí fēngqì.
column7: This school has a good atmosphere of study.
column9: The shared mood or habits of a school, workplace or era, good or bad: 社會風氣, 學習風氣, 不良風氣, 敗壞風氣. It is not the weather and not one person's habit.

column3: Praise for a person's talk: 说话风趣, 风趣的人. It means witty with ease and charm, a warmer word than 幽默. 风 in this sense of style is also in 风格, 风度 and 风味.
column4: 他讲话很风趣，大家都喜欢他。
column5: 他講話很風趣，大家都喜歡他。
column6: Tā jiǎnghuà hěn fēngqù, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
column7: He talks wittily and everybody likes him.
column9: Praise for a person's talk: 說話風趣, 風趣的人. It means witty with ease and charm, a warmer word than 幽默. 風 in this sense of style is also in 風格, 風度 and 風味.

column3: Rude if said of a person with a mental illness, but a common exaggeration for someone wild or reckless: 你是疯子吗？ 子 makes words for kinds of people, often blunt: 傻子, 骗子, 瞎子.
column6: Tā kāichē xiàng fēngzi yīyàng kuài.
column7: He drives as fast as a madman.
column9: Rude if said of a person with a mental illness, but a common exaggeration for someone wild or reckless: 你是瘋子嗎？ 子 makes words for kinds of people, often blunt: 傻子, 騙子, 瞎子.

column3: The everyday word for pink: it goes before a noun or 的, and 粉红色 is the color name. 粉红泡泡 is slang for a dreamy, romantic mood. The earliest sense of 粉 is believed to be face powder; it later also named the pink of a face wearing it.
column4: 她今天穿了一条粉红的裙子。
column5: 她今天穿了一條粉紅的裙子。
column6: Tā jīntiān chuān le yī tiáo fěnhóng de qúnzi.
column7: She wore a pink skirt today.
column9: The everyday word for pink: it goes before a noun or 的, and 粉紅色 is the color name. 粉紅泡泡 is slang for a dreamy, romantic mood. The earliest sense of 粉 is believed to be face powder; it later also named the pink of a face wearing it.

column3: Mostly an adverb for what is plain to see although someone says otherwise, so it carries a note of blame or protest: 分明是你。 As an adjective it means clearly distinct, as in 黑白分明.
column4: 你分明知道，为什么说不知道？
column5: 你分明知道，為什麼說不知道？
column6: Nǐ fēnmíng zhīdào, wèishénme shuō bù zhīdào?
column7: You clearly know, so why do you say you don't?
column9: Mostly an adverb for what is plain to see although someone says otherwise, so it carries a note of blame or protest: 分明是你。 As an adjective it means clearly distinct, as in 黑白分明.

column3: A strong, written word for anger at something unjust, such as an event or a decision, more than a personal flare-up (that is 生气). Common with 感到, 令人 and 对…感到愤怒.
column4: 大家对这件事感到非常愤怒。
column5: 大家對這件事感到非常憤怒。
column6: Dàjiā duì zhè jiàn shì gǎndào fēicháng fènnù.
column7: Everyone is very angry about this matter.
column9: A strong, written word for anger at something unjust, such as an event or a decision, more than a personal flare-up (that is 生氣). Common with 感到, 令人 and 對…感到憤怒.

column3: On its own it is the verb for being convinced or admiring someone: 我不服 'I won't accept it', 我服了你 'I give up, you win'. For clothes it appears only in compounds such as 衣服 and 制服.
column6: Nǐ zhēn lìhai, wǒ fú le.
column7: You are really good; I give up.
column9: On its own it is the verb for being convinced or admiring someone: 我不服 'I won't accept it', 我服了你 'I give up, you win'. For clothes it appears only in compounds such as 衣服 and 制服.

column3: Besides floating on water or in the air (浮起来), it describes shallow or restless people and attitudes: 浮躁 'restless, impatient', 浮夸 'exaggerated, showy'.
column6: Shùyè fú zài shuǐmiàn shàng.
column7: Leaves float on the surface of the water.
column9: Besides floating on water or in the air (浮起來), it describes shallow or restless people and attitudes: 浮躁 'restless, impatient', 浮誇 'exaggerated, showy'.

column3: Written and formal: going to a place or an event for a purpose, with the place or event right after it, as in 赴美, 赴约 and 赴宴. In speech you say 去.
column6: Tā míngnián yào fù Měiguó liúxué.
column7: Next year he will go to America to study.
column9: Written and formal: going to a place or an event for a purpose, with the place or event right after it, as in 赴美, 赴約 and 赴宴. In speech you say 去.

column3: As a measure word it counts things that come as a pair or a set: 眼镜, 手套, 扑克牌. Before a title it makes the deputy: 副总统, 副经理. It is also in 副作用 'side effect' and 副词 'adverb'.
column6: Tā dàizhe yī fù hēikuàng yǎnjìng.
column7: He wears a pair of black-framed glasses.
column9: As a measure word it counts things that come as a pair or a set: 眼鏡, 手套, 撲克牌. Before a title it makes the deputy: 副總統, 副經理. It is also in 副作用 'side effect' and 副詞 'adverb'.

column3: A teacher or tutor helping someone study: 辅导功课, 课后辅导. It also covers counseling and coaching, as in 心理辅导, and 辅导老师 is a counselor or coach.
column4: 老师每天放学后辅导我们功课。
column5: 老師每天放學後輔導我們功課。
column6: Lǎoshī měitiān fàngxué hòu fǔdǎo wǒmen gōngkè.
column7: The teacher tutors us in our schoolwork every day after school.
column9: A teacher or tutor helping someone study: 輔導功課, 課後輔導. It also covers counseling and coaching, as in 心理輔導, and 輔導老師 is a counselor or coach.

column3: Goes before a noun for something tacked on to the main thing: 附加条件, 附加费 'surcharge', 附加价值 'added value'. Formal, and common in contracts, rules and price lists.
column4: 这个活动有一些附加条件。
column5: 這個活動有一些附加條件。
column6: Zhège huódòng yǒu yīxiē fùjiā tiáojiàn.
column7: This event has some additional conditions.
column9: Goes before a noun for something tacked on to the main thing: 附加條件, 附加費 'surcharge', 附加價值 'added value'. Formal, and common in contracts, rules and price lists.

column3: Women as a group, in official and social contexts: 妇女节, 妇女权益, 妇女团体. It is the word of laws and news; for a woman in ordinary talk say 女人, and for girls 女孩.
column4: 政府推出了保护妇女的新办法。
column5: 政府推出了保護婦女的新辦法。
column6: Zhèngfǔ tuīchū le bǎohù fùnǚ de xīn bànfǎ.
column7: The government has introduced new measures to protect women.
column9: Women as a group, in official and social contexts: 婦女節, 婦女權益, 婦女團體. It is the word of laws and news; for a woman in ordinary talk say 女人, and for girls 女孩.

column3: Describes a family, a region or a way of life that has plenty: 生活富裕, 变得富裕. It is neutral to formal; calling a person rich in speech is blunter, 有钱.
column6: Tāmen jiā de shēnghuó hěn fùyù.
column7: Their family lives in comfort.
column9: Describes a family, a region or a way of life that has plenty: 生活富裕, 變得富裕. It is neutral to formal; calling a person rich in speech is blunter, 有錢.

column3: The thing that closes a pot, bottle or box: 锅盖子, 打开盖子. The verb 盖 'to cover' (盖好) makes it, and the same 盖 also means to build a house: 盖房子.
column4: 请把盖子盖好，不然汤会凉。
column5: 請把蓋子蓋好，不然湯會涼。
column6: Qǐng bǎ gàizi gài hǎo, bùrán tāng huì liáng.
column7: Please put the lid on, or the soup will get cold.
column9: The thing that closes a pot, bottle or box: 鍋蓋子, 打開蓋子. The verb 蓋 'to cover' (蓋好) makes it, and the same 蓋 also means to build a house: 蓋房子.

column3: The organ and the food: 肝脏 in medical talk, 猪肝 on the plate, 肝炎 hepatitis. In slang 爆肝 is working or gaming until your health pays for it.
column6: Hē tài duō jiǔ duì gān bù hǎo.
column7: Drinking too much alcohol is bad for the liver.
column9: The organ and the food: 肝臟 in medical talk, 豬肝 on the plate, 肝炎 hepatitis. In slang 爆肝 is working or gaming until your health pays for it.

column3: On the mainland it is an official or manager of the Party or state; in Taiwan it more often means the officers who run a club or group, as in 社团干部. Both sides say 学生干部 for student officers.
column6: Tā shì xuéshēnghuì de gànbù.
column7: He is an officer of the student council.
column9: On the mainland it is an official or manager of the Party or state; in Taiwan it more often means the officers who run a club or group, as in 社團幹部. Both sides say 學生幹部 for student officers.

column3: Gratitude for kindness or care received, warmer and more formal than 谢谢: 感恩的心, 懂得感恩. It takes the giver or the deed as object: 感恩父母. 感恩节 is Thanksgiving.
column4: 我们应该感恩父母的养育。
column5: 我們應該感恩父母的養育。
column6: Wǒmen yīnggāi gǎn'ēn fùmǔ de yǎngyù.
column7: We should be grateful for what our parents did in raising us.
column9: Gratitude for kindness or care received, warmer and more formal than 謝謝: 感恩的心, 懂得感恩. It takes the giver or the deed as object: 感恩父母. 感恩節 is Thanksgiving.

column3: Mostly in compounds for steel things: 钢铁, 钢笔 'fountain pen', 钢琴 'piano', 钢筋 'rebar', 不锈钢 'stainless steel'. Figuratively it means unyielding, as in 钢铁般的意志.
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo shì yòng gāng zuò de.
column7: This bridge is made of steel.
column9: Mostly in compounds for steel things: 鋼鐵, 鋼筆 'fountain pen', 鋼琴 'piano', 鋼筋 'rebar', 不鏽鋼 'stainless steel'. Figuratively it means unyielding, as in 鋼鐵般的意志.

column3: The everyday name for the Hong Kong dollar; the official name is 港元. A pattern for currencies: place + 币, as in 人民币, 台币 and 韩币.
column4: 我想把人民币换成港币。
column5: 我想把人民幣換成港幣。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ Rénmínbì huàn chéng Gǎngbì.
column7: I want to change yuan into Hong Kong dollars.
column9: The everyday name for the Hong Kong dollar; the official name is 港元. A pattern for currencies: place + 幣, as in 人民幣, 台幣 and 韓幣.

column3: The everyday word for a port, since 港 alone is rare in speech outside names such as 香港. Common in 港口城市 'port city' and 进出港口; a fishing harbor is 渔港.
column4: 这个港口每天都有很多船进出。
column5: 這個港口每天都有很多船進出。
column6: Zhège gǎngkǒu měitiān dōu yǒu hěn duō chuán jìnchū.
column7: Many ships come and go at this port every day.
column9: The everyday word for a port, since 港 alone is rare in speech outside names such as 香港. Common in 港口城市 'port city' and 進出港口; a fishing harbor is 漁港.

column3: Hardly used alone for a harbor in speech; it works in compounds: 渔港 'fishing harbor', 港湾 'bay', 出港 'leave port'. As the short name for Hong Kong it joins other words: 港币, 港星 'Hong Kong star'.
column4: 这个港口每天都有很多船。
column5: 這個港口每天都有很多船。
column6: Zhège gǎng kǒu měitiān dōu yǒu hěn duō chuán.
column7: This port has many boats every day.
column9: Hardly used alone for a harbor in speech; it works in compounds: 漁港 'fishing harbor', 港灣 'bay', 出港 'leave port'. As the short name for Hong Kong it joins other words: 港幣, 港星 'Hong Kong star'.

column3: A strong, heartfelt thanks for specific help, more serious than 谢谢: 非常感激, 深表感激. 感谢 is the more neutral formal 'thank', while 感激 stresses the feeling.
column6: Wǒ fēicháng gǎnjī nǐ de bāngzhù.
column7: I am very grateful for your help.
column9: A strong, heartfelt thanks for specific help, more serious than 謝謝: 非常感激, 深表感激. 感謝 is the more neutral formal 'thank', while 感激 stresses the feeling.

column3: Casual speech, short for 干什么: either 'what are you doing?' (你干嘛？) or 'why?' before a verb (干嘛不去？). It can sound impatient or sharp. On the mainland it is also written 干吗.
column6: Nǐ gànmá yīzhí kàn wǒ?
column7: Why do you keep looking at me?
column9: Casual speech, short for 幹什麼: either 'what are you doing?' (你幹嘛？) or 'why?' before a verb (幹嘛不去？). It can sound impatient or sharp. On the mainland it is also written 幹嗎.

column3: Used for catching an infection (感染病毒, 伤口感染) and also for a mood passing from person to person: 被他的笑容感染 'be won over by his smile'. Both senses often take 被.
column4: 他被病毒感染了，需要休息。
column5: 他被病毒感染了，需要休息。
column6: Tā bèi bìngdú gǎnrǎn le, xūyào xiūxi.
column7: He has been infected by a virus and needs rest.
column9: Used for catching an infection (感染病毒, 傷口感染) and also for a mood passing from person to person: 被他的笑容感染 'be won over by his smile'. Both senses often take 被.

column3: Mostly bound, as in 告诉, 告别 and 报告. As a bare verb it means to sue or report someone: 我要去告他, 告上法院. The same 告 is in 原告 'plaintiff' and 被告 'defendant'.
column4: 他做了坏事，我要去告他。
column5: 他做了壞事，我要去告他。
column6: Tā zuò le huài shì, wǒ yào qù gào tā.
column7: He did something bad, and I am going to report him.
column9: Mostly bound, as in 告訴, 告別 and 報告. As a bare verb it means to sue or report someone: 我要去告他, 告上法院. The same 告 is in 原告 'plaintiff' and 被告 'defendant'.

column3: A polite, slightly formal way for a guest to say goodbye to the host, said by the one who leaves: 我该告辞了. For a casual goodbye among friends say 我先走了 or 再见.
column4: 时间不早了，我该告辞了。
column5: 時間不早了，我該告辭了。
column6: Shíjiān bù zǎo le, wǒ gāi gàocí le.
column7: It is getting late and I must be going.
column9: A polite, slightly formal way for a guest to say goodbye to the host, said by the one who leaves: 我該告辭了. For a casual goodbye among friends say 我先走了 or 再見.

column3: Besides a mountain peak, it is the busiest time or the highest point: 上下班高峰 'commuting rush hour', 高峰期, 交通高峰. Its opposite is 低谷, as in 经济低谷.
column4: 下班高峰时，路上车很多。
column5: 下班高峰時，路上車很多。
column6: Xiàbān gāofēng shí, lùshang chē hěn duō.
column7: At the evening rush hour, there are many cars on the road.
column9: Besides a mountain peak, it is the busiest time or the highest point: 上下班高峰 'commuting rush hour', 高峰期, 交通高峰. Its opposite is 低谷, as in 經濟低谷.

column3: Praises a person's bearing or an object's fine quality, a sense of class and refinement: 高贵的气质. It has nothing to do with price: expensive is plain 贵.
column6: Tā kàn qǐlái hěn gāoguì.
column7: She looks very elegant.
column9: Praises a person's bearing or an object's fine quality, a sense of class and refinement: 高貴的氣質. It has nothing to do with price: expensive is plain 貴.

column3: Praises a clever plan or move, or a person's skill in a profession: 高明的办法, 医术高明, 你真高明. It sounds a little formal and appreciative.
column6: Nǐ zhège bànfǎ zhēn gāomíng.
column7: This method of yours is really clever.
column9: Praises a clever plan or move, or a person's skill in a profession: 高明的辦法, 醫術高明, 你真高明. It sounds a little formal and appreciative.

column3: Someone far ahead of others in a skill or game: 电脑高手, 围棋高手, 武林高手. 手 names a person skilled at something in other words too: 新手 'beginner', 老手 'veteran', 歌手 'singer'.
column4: 他是我们公司的电脑高手。
column5: 他是我們公司的電腦高手。
column6: Tā shì wǒmen gōngsī de diànnǎo gāoshǒu.
column7: He is the computer expert of our company.
column9: Someone far ahead of others in a skill or game: 電腦高手, 圍棋高手, 武林高手. 手 names a person skilled at something in other words too: 新手 'beginner', 老手 'veteran', 歌手 'singer'.

column3: Cutting with a blade or sickle, as grass, crops or skin: 割草, 割伤 'cut oneself'. For slicing food with a knife say 切, and for cutting with scissors 剪.
column6: Bàba zài yuànzi lǐ gē cǎo.
column7: Dad is mowing the grass in the yard.
column9: Cutting with a blade or sickle, as grass, crops or skin: 割草, 割傷 'cut oneself'. For slicing food with a knife say 切, and for cutting with scissors 剪.

column3: A colloquial 'put' that stresses setting something down and leaving it: 搁在桌上. It also means to add a seasoning (汤里搁点盐) and to put aside or delay: 事情先搁着, 耽搁 'to hold up'.
column4: 他把书搁在桌子上就出去了。
column5: 他把書擱在桌子上就出去了。
column6: Tā bǎ shū gē zài zhuōzi shàng jiù chūqù le.
column7: He put the book on the table and went out.
column9: A colloquial 'put' that stresses setting something down and leaving it: 擱在桌上. It also means to add a seasoning (湯裡擱點鹽) and to put aside or delay: 事情先擱著, 耽擱 'to hold up'.

column3: More written and solemn than the everyday 唱歌, often for praising or for a chorus: 歌唱祖国, 放声歌唱, 歌唱比赛. 歌唱家 is a professional singer.
column4: 孩子们在台上快乐地歌唱。
column5: 孩子們在台上快樂地歌唱。
column6: Háizimen zài tái shàng kuàilè de gēchàng.
column7: The children sing happily on the stage.
column9: More written and solemn than the everyday 唱歌, often for praising or for a chorus: 歌唱祖國, 放聲歌唱, 歌唱比賽. 歌唱家 is a professional singer.

column3: A four-character phrase for 'in every field', mostly before 的人 or before 都: 各行各业的人, 各行各业都需要。 The pattern 各 + noun + 各 + noun means 'every X and every Y'. Here 行 is read háng, the reading for a line of business, and not xíng 'to walk'.
column4: 各行各业的人都来参加了。
column5: 各行各業的人都來參加了。
column6: Gèhánggèyè de rén dōu lái cānjiā le.
column7: People from every walk of life came to join.
column9: A four-character phrase for 'in every field', mostly before 的人 or before 都: 各行各業的人, 各行各業都需要。 The pattern 各 + noun + 各 + noun means 'every X and every Y'. Here 行 is read háng, the reading for a line of business, and not xíng 'to walk'.

column3: Chinese opera is another thing: 京剧 'Beijing opera', and in Taiwan 歌仔戏 'Taiwanese opera'. 剧 is in other kinds of drama too: 话剧 'stage play', 电视剧 'TV series', 喜剧 'comedy'.
column4: 我们昨天晚上去看了歌剧。
column5: 我們昨天晚上去看了歌劇。
column6: Wǒmen zuótiān wǎnshang qù kàn le gējù.
column7: We went to see an opera last night.
column9: Chinese opera is another thing: 京劇 'Beijing opera', and in Taiwan 歌仔戲 'Taiwanese opera'. 劇 is in other kinds of drama too: 話劇 'stage play', 電視劇 'TV series', 喜劇 'comedy'.

column3: Goes with what is supplied: 供电, 供水, 供暖. 供应 is 'to supply', and 供不应求 means supply falls short of demand. It can also mean 'for the use of': 供大家使用.
column4: 这个水库供全市的人用水。
column5: 這個水庫供全市的人用水。
column6: Zhège shuǐkù gōng quán shì de rén yòng shuǐ.
column7: This reservoir supplies water to the whole city.
column9: Goes with what is supplied: 供電, 供水, 供暖. 供應 is 'to supply', and 供不應求 means supply falls short of demand. It can also mean 'for the use of': 供大家使用.

column3: The in-law term, said by a married woman about her husband's father: 我公公. His mother is 婆婆, and 公婆 means the couple together. A husband's word for his wife's father is 岳父. 公 can also mean a male of an older generation or higher rank, and, of animals, a male.
column6: Wǒ gōnggong hěn xǐhuan zhòng cài.
column7: My father-in-law likes growing vegetables.
column9: The in-law term, said by a married woman about her husband's father: 我公公. His mother is 婆婆, and 公婆 means the couple together. A husband's word for his wife's father is 岳父. 公 can also mean a male of an older generation or higher rank, and, of animals, a male.

column3: It names the organization, and its members are 会员: 加入工会, 工会代表. 会 as a suffix means an association in many words: 学生会, 商会, 协会.
column6: Tā shì gōnghuì de dàibiǎo.
column7: He is the union's representative.
column9: It names the organization, and its members are 會員: 加入工會, 工會代表. 會 as a suffix means an association in many words: 學生會, 商會, 協會.

column3: Said of schools and hospitals run by the government: 公立学校, 公立医院; the opposite is 私立. The first character says who runs it: 国立 national, 市立 city-run.
column6: Zhè suǒ gōnglì xuéxiào hěn dà.
column7: This public school is big.
column9: Said of schools and hospitals run by the government: 公立學校, 公立醫院; the opposite is 私立. The first character says who runs it: 國立 national, 市立 city-run.

column3: Spoken: pay for a piece of work or a day's labor, such as a helper or repair person gets: 付工钱, 工钱怎么算. Regular monthly pay is 工资 or 薪水.
column6: Lǎobǎn hái méi fù gōngqián.
column7: The boss hasn't paid the wages yet.
column9: Spoken: pay for a piece of work or a day's labor, such as a helper or repair person gets: 付工錢, 工錢怎麼算. Regular monthly pay is 工資 or 薪水.

column3: For a thing shared by everyone: 公用电话, 公用厕所, 公用设备. For public places and services, 公共 is the word: 公共场所, 公共交通.
column6: Zhè shì gōngyòng de diànhuà.
column7: This is a public telephone.
column9: For a thing shared by everyone: 公用電話, 公用廁所, 公用設備. For public places and services, 公共 is the word: 公共場所, 公共交通.

column3: Sent at the post office with 寄挂号信. 挂号 alone is the verb 'to register': for mail, and more often for checking in at a hospital before seeing a doctor: 去医院挂号.
column4: 这封挂号信是寄给你的。
column5: 這封掛號信是寄給你的。
column6: Zhè fēng guàhàoxìn shì jì gěi nǐ de.
column7: This registered letter was sent to you.
column9: Sent at the post office with 寄掛號信. 掛號 alone is the verb 'to register': for mail, and more often for checking in at a hospital before seeing a doctor: 去醫院掛號.

column3: Said when you have just learned the reason for something. The explanation can follow or come first: 怪不得你这么累，原来你昨天没睡。 难怪 means the same.
column6: Guàibude tā zhème gāoxìng.
column7: No wonder he is so happy.
column9: Said when you have just learned the reason for something. The explanation can follow or come first: 怪不得你這麼累，原來你昨天沒睡。 難怪 means the same.

column3: Mostly negative with a verb, for what you can't get used to: 吃不惯, 住不惯, 看不惯 'can't stand the sight of'. It also means to spoil a child: 惯着孩子, 惯坏了.
column6: Nǐ bié bǎ háizi guàn huài le.
column7: Don't spoil the child.
column9: Mostly negative with a verb, for what you can't get used to: 吃不慣, 住不慣, 看不慣 'can't stand the sight of'. It also means to spoil a child: 慣著孩子, 慣壞了.

column3: The container itself: 糖罐子, 玻璃罐子. 罐 also counts what a container holds: 一罐糖, 一罐啤酒. The canned food in it is 罐头.
column6: Guànzi lǐ zhuāngmǎn le táng.
column7: The jar is full of sugar.
column9: The container itself: 糖罐子, 玻璃罐子. 罐 also counts what a container holds: 一罐糖, 一罐啤酒. The canned food in it is 罐頭.

column3: Used for oil and gas lines (输油管道) and figuratively for a way to get something done: 合法管道, 沟通管道. The figurative use is heard more in Taiwan, where the mainland often says 渠道.
column6: Dìxià de guǎndào huài le.
column7: The pipes underground are broken.
column9: Used for oil and gas lines (輸油管道) and figuratively for a way to get something done: 合法管道, 溝通管道. The figurative use is heard more in Taiwan, where the mainland often says 渠道.

column3: For wide stretches of land or sea (广阔的草原) and figuratively for range: 视野广阔, 前景广阔 'broad prospects'. 宽阔 is for width of roads, rivers and rooms.
column6: Cǎoyuán fēicháng guǎngkuò.
column7: The grassland is very vast.
column9: For wide stretches of land or sea (廣闊的草原) and figuratively for range: 視野廣闊, 前景廣闊 'broad prospects'. 寬闊 is for width of roads, rivers and rooms.

column3: An adjective for something shiny or well lit (光亮的地板) and also a noun for a glimmer of light: 一点光亮. For a room full of daylight, 明亮 is the more natural word.
column6: Yuǎn chù chūxiàn le yī diǎn guāngliàng.
column7: A little light appeared in the distance.
column9: An adjective for something shiny or well lit (光亮的地板) and also a noun for a glimmer of light: 一點光亮. For a room full of daylight, 明亮 is the more natural word.

column3: An adverb placed before a noun or verb phrase to say that this alone is already a lot, usually answered by 就: 光是…就…. This 光 has nothing to do with light.
column6: Guāngshì jīpiào jiù yào yī wàn kuài.
column7: The plane ticket alone costs ten thousand dollars.
column9: An adverb placed before a noun or verb phrase to say that this alone is already a lot, usually answered by 就: 光是…就…. This 光 has nothing to do with light.

column3: The usual word for tourism in Taiwan (观光客, 观光景点, 观光局), both noun and verb; on the mainland 旅游 is the more common word, and 观光 turns up in 观光车 and 观光巴士.
column4: 这座城市每年吸引很多人来观光。
column5: 這座城市每年吸引很多人來觀光。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì měi nián xīyǐn hěn duō rén lái guānguāng.
column7: This city attracts many people to visit as tourists every year.
column9: The usual word for tourism in Taiwan (觀光客, 觀光景點, 觀光局), both noun and verb; on the mainland 旅遊 is the more common word, and 觀光 turns up in 觀光車 and 觀光巴士.

column3: What is normally done in an organization or a field: 按照惯例, 打破惯例, 国际惯例. It is firmer than 习惯, which describes one person's habit.
column6: Ànzhào guànlì, wǒmen xiān kāihuì.
column7: As usual, we hold a meeting first.
column9: What is normally done in an organization or a field: 按照慣例, 打破慣例, 國際慣例. It is firmer than 習慣, which describes one person's habit.

column3: Canned food or the can itself: 开罐头, 凤梨罐头. 'Canned' also means prefabricated or prerecorded, as in 罐头笑声 'laugh track'.
column4: 他带了几个罐头去露营。
column5: 他帶了幾個罐頭去露營。
column6: Tā dài le jǐ ge guàntou qù lùyíng.
column7: He took a few cans of food camping.
column9: Canned food or the can itself: 開罐頭, 鳳梨罐頭. 'Canned' also means prefabricated or prerecorded, as in 罐頭笑聲 'laugh track'.

column3: Official, a person with a position in government or a large organization: 政府官员, 高级官员, 外交官员. 官 shows a roof 宀 over a building where officials work, and 员 means a person in a role (演员, 公务员). It is neutral to formal.
column4: 政府官员今天开了记者会。
column5: 政府官員今天開了記者會。
column6: Zhèngfǔ guānyuán jīntiān kāi le jìzhěhuì.
column7: Government officials held a press conference today.
column9: Official, a person with a position in government or a large organization: 政府官員, 高級官員, 外交官員. 官 shows a roof 宀 over a building where officials work, and 員 means a person in a role (演員, 公務員). It is neutral to formal.

column3: To control, restrict, by the authorities: 交通管制 "traffic control", 管制进口, 管制药品 "controlled drugs", 管制区. It is about rules imposed from above, closer to "regulate and limit" than to just "manage" (管理).
column6: Zhè tiáo lù jīntiān jiāotōng guǎnzhì.
column7: Traffic on this road is controlled today.
column9: To control, restrict, by the authorities: 交通管制 "traffic control", 管制進口, 管制藥品 "controlled drugs", 管制區. It is about rules imposed from above, closer to "regulate and limit" than to just "manage" (管理).

column3: Melon seeds, really the roasted, salted seeds of watermelon, pumpkin or sunflower that people crack open with their teeth as a snack: 嗑瓜子. 瓜 is a picture of a melon hanging from its vine. The dictionary reads the last syllable zǐ here.
column4: 看电视的时候，他喜欢嗑瓜子。
column5: 看電視的時候，他喜歡嗑瓜子。
column6: Kàn diànshì de shíhou, tā xǐhuan kè guāzǐ.
column7: When he watches TV, he likes to crack melon seeds.
column9: Melon seeds, really the roasted, salted seeds of watermelon, pumpkin or sunflower that people crack open with their teeth as a snack: 嗑瓜子. 瓜 is a picture of a melon hanging from its vine. The dictionary reads the last syllable zǐ here.

column3: Lonely, the feeling of being alone: 感到孤单, 一个人很孤单. Compare 寂寞, which stresses an inner emptiness; 孤单 is more about having nobody beside you. 孤 has 子 "child" and 瓜 for the sound (not alike now), and recalls the orphan; 单 is "single".
column4: 一个人在国外，他觉得很孤单。
column5: 一個人在國外，他覺得很孤單。
column6: Yī ge rén zài guówài, tā juéde hěn gūdān.
column7: Alone abroad, he feels lonely.
column9: Lonely, the feeling of being alone: 感到孤單, 一個人很孤單. Compare 寂寞, which stresses an inner emptiness; 孤單 is more about having nobody beside you. 孤 has 子 "child" and 瓜 for the sound (not alike now), and recalls the orphan; 單 is "single".

column3: Classical, of art, music, literature, style: 古典音乐, 古典文学, 古典舞, 古典美. It points to the old, established tradition. 典 shows two hands holding a book 册 on a stand, an authoritative text, as in 字典 "dictionary".
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan tīng gǔdiǎn yīnyuè.
column7: I like listening to classical music.
column9: Classical, of art, music, literature, style: 古典音樂, 古典文學, 古典舞, 古典美. It points to the old, established tradition. 典 shows two hands holding a book 冊 on a stand, an authoritative text, as in 字典 "dictionary".

column3: To kneel: 跪下, 下跪, 跪着, 跪在地上; also in 跪坐 "sit on one's heels", as in a Japanese tatami room. 足 "foot" is the meaning part, and 危 gives a sound that has since drifted (wēi, guì). It also turns up in internet slang for "I give up".
column6: Tā guì xiàlái xiàng tā qiúhūn.
column7: He knelt down to propose to her.
column9: To kneel: 跪下, 下跪, 跪著, 跪在地上; also in 跪坐 "sit on one's heels", as in a Japanese tatami room. 足 "foot" is the meaning part, and 危 gives a sound that has since drifted (wēi, guì). It also turns up in internet slang for "I give up".

column3: Counter in a shop, bank or at a check-in desk: 服务柜台, 柜台人员, 去柜台结账. 柜 has 木 "wood" and 巨 for the sound, because a cabinet is made of wood. 台 is the "platform" in 舞台 and 电台.
column6: Qǐng dào guìtái fù qián.
column7: Please pay at the counter.
column9: Counter in a shop, bank or at a check-in desk: 服務櫃臺, 櫃臺人員, 去櫃臺結帳. 櫃 has 木 "wood" and 貴 for the sound (guì, the same), because a cabinet is made of wood. 臺 is the "platform" in 舞臺 and 電臺.

column3: Nobility, aristocrat: 欧洲贵族, 贵族家庭, 贵族血统. It also gives a flavor of luxury, as in 贵族学校, a pricey private school with a posh image. 贵 "noble, expensive" + 族 "clan, group"; 族 shows a flag 方 and an arrow 矢, a group that gathers under one banner.
column4: 这座城堡以前是贵族的家。
column5: 這座城堡以前是貴族的家。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngbǎo yǐqián shì guìzú de jiā.
column7: This castle used to be a nobleman's home.
column9: Nobility, aristocrat: 歐洲貴族, 貴族家庭, 貴族血統. It also gives a flavor of luxury, as in 貴族學校, a pricey private school with a posh image. 貴 "noble, expensive" + 族 "clan, group"; 族 shows a flag 方 and an arrow 矢, a group that gathers under one banner.

column3: To wrap, bundle up: 裹着毯子 "wrapped in a blanket", 裹起来, 包裹 "parcel". It means wrapping something around a body or an object. 衣 "clothes" is the meaning part, and 果 gives the sound (guǒ, the same); the character puts 果 inside 衣.
column4: 天冷，他裹着毯子看电视。
column5: 天冷，他裹著毯子看電視。
column6: Tiān lěng, tā guǒ zhe tǎnzi kàn diànshì.
column7: It's cold, so he watches TV wrapped in a blanket.
column9: To wrap, bundle up: 裹著毯子 "wrapped in a blanket", 裹起來, 包裹 "parcel". It means wrapping something around a body or an object. 衣 "clothes" is the meaning part, and 果 gives the sound (guǒ, the same); the character puts 果 inside 衣.

column3: Pot, pan: a cooking pot with a handle, as in 煮饭的锅子, 炒菜锅子. Also in 火锅 "hotpot". 锅 has 金 "metal" and 呙, the same sound part as in 过 and 祸. 呙 is no longer pronounced like any of the three (guō, guò, huò). 子 is neutral.
column6: Guōzi lǐ yǒu rè tāng.
column7: There is hot soup in the pot.
column9: Pot, pan: a cooking pot with a handle, as in 煮飯的鍋子, 炒菜鍋子. Also in 火鍋 "hotpot". 鍋 has 金 "metal" and 咼, the same sound part as in 過 and 禍. 咼 is no longer pronounced like any of the three (guō, guò, huò). 子 is neutral.

column3: Transition, the stage between two states: 过渡期 "transition period", 过渡阶段, 过渡政府. As a verb, "to cross over" water. 渡 has 氵 "water" and 度 for the sound (dù, the same), a crossing of a river. 过 "pass" + 渡 "cross".
column4: 这只是一个过渡的办法。
column5: 這只是一個過渡的辦法。
column6: Zhè zhǐ shì yī ge guòdù de bànfǎ.
column7: This is only a temporary solution.
column9: Transition, the stage between two states: 過渡期 "transition period", 過渡階段, 過渡政府. As a verb, "to cross over" water. 渡 has 氵 "water" and 度 for the sound (dù, the same), a crossing of a river. 過 "pass" + 渡 "cross".

column3: National legislature, parliament: 美国国会 "the U.S. Congress", 国会议员. Taiwan's own body is the 立法院, but 国会 is the word for the institution in general: 国会改革. 国 "country" + 会 "assembly".
column4: 美国国会通过了新法律。
column5: 美國國會通過了新法律。
column6: Měiguó guóhuì tōngguò le xīn fǎlǜ.
column7: The U.S. Congress passed a new law.
column9: National legislature, parliament: 美國國會 "the U.S. Congress", 國會議員. Taiwan's own body is the 立法院, but 國會 is the word for the institution in general: 國會改革. 國 "country" + 會 "assembly".

column3: National, set up and run by the state, of universities and museums: 国立大学, 国立故宫博物院, 国立台湾大学. It is a part of many official names in Taiwan. The opposites are 私立 and 市立.
column6: Tā kǎoshàng le guólì dàxué.
column7: He got into a national university.
column9: National, set up and run by the state, of universities and museums: 國立大學, 國立故宮博物院, 國立臺灣大學. It is a part of many official names in Taiwan. The opposites are 私立 and 市立.

column3: To celebrate a holiday, mainly Chinese festivals such as the Lunar New Year and the Mid-Autumn Festival: 过节回家, 过节的气氛. 过 here is "to spend, to celebrate" (as in 过年), and 节 "festival". In another sense, 过节 is an old grudge.
column4: 过节的时候，全家人都回来了。
column5: 過節的時候，全家人都回來了。
column6: Guòjié de shíhou, quánjiārén dōu huílái le.
column7: At the holiday, the whole family came home.
column9: To celebrate a holiday, mainly Chinese festivals such as the Lunar New Year and the Mid-Autumn Festival: 過節回家, 過節的氣氛. 過 here is "to spend, to celebrate" (as in 過年), and 節 "festival". In another sense, 過節 is an old grudge.

column3: To filter: 过滤水, 过滤网, 过滤杂质 "filter out impurities". It is also used for information: 过滤资讯, 过滤垃圾邮件 "filter spam". 滤 has 氵 "water" and 虑 for the sound (lǜ, the same).
column6: Zhè tái jīqì kěyǐ guòlǜ shuǐ.
column7: This machine can filter water.
column9: To filter: 過濾水, 過濾網, 過濾雜質 "filter out impurities". It is also used for information: 過濾資訊, 過濾垃圾郵件 "filter spam". 濾 has 氵 "water" and 慮 for the sound (lǜ, the same).

column3: National flag: 升国旗 "raise the flag", 挂国旗, 国旗飘扬. 旗 has 㫃 "flag" for the meaning and 其 for the sound (qí, the same).
column6: Xuéxiào měi tiān zǎoshang shēng guóqí.
column7: The school raises the flag every morning.
column9: National flag: 升國旗 "raise the flag", 掛國旗, 國旗飄揚. 旗 has 㫃 "flag" for the meaning and 其 for the sound (qí, the same).

column3: To expire, be overdue: 过期牛奶, 护照过期, 过期不候 "no waiting after the deadline". It is the standard word for expired food, a visa or a coupon. 过 "pass" + 期 "term, date". 期 has 月 "moon" and 其 for the sound.
column6: Zhè píng niúnǎi yǐjīng guòqí le.
column7: This bottle of milk has expired.
column9: To expire, be overdue: 過期牛奶, 護照過期, 過期不候 "no waiting after the deadline". It is the standard word for expired food, a visa or a coupon. 過 "pass" + 期 "term, date". 期 has 月 "moon" and 其 for the sound.

column3: To pass away, a gentle word for death, used about someone you know, usually an older person: 他的爷爷去年过世了. It softens what 死 states bluntly, and is polite in condolences. 过 "pass" + 世 "world, life".
column6: Tā de yéye qùnián guòshì le.
column7: His grandfather passed away last year.
column9: To pass away, a gentle word for death, used about someone you know, usually an older person: 他的爺爺去年過世了. It softens what 死 states bluntly, and is polite in condolences. 過 "pass" + 世 "world, life".

column3: In Taiwan, "junior high school", short for 国民中学, grades seven to nine: 国中生, 上国中. It sits between 国小 (elementary school) and 高中 (senior high). The mainland says 初中.
column6: Wǒ dìdi jīnnián shàng guózhōng.
column7: My younger brother starts junior high this year.
column9: In Taiwan, "junior high school", short for 國民中學, grades seven to nine: 國中生, 上國中. It sits between 國小 (elementary school) and 高中 (senior high). The mainland says 初中.

column3: Bone: 骨头 "bone", 骨折 "fracture", 骨科 "orthopedics", 骨瘦如柴 "skin and bones". 骨 has a bone shape 冎 on top and 肉 "flesh" (⺼) added under it. The word 骨头 has a neutral second syllable.
column6: Gǒu zài kěn yī gēn gǔtou.
column7: The dog is gnawing a bone.
column9: Bone: 骨頭 "bone", 骨折 "fracture", 骨科 "orthopedics", 骨瘦如柴 "skin and bones". 骨 has a bone shape 冎 on top and 肉 "flesh" (⺼) added under it. The word 骨頭 has a neutral second syllable.

column3: To inspire, encourage, boost morale: 受到鼓舞, 鼓舞士气, 令人鼓舞 "encouraging". The person is lifted up in spirit. 鼓 "drum" + 舞 "dance": drums and dancing lift a crowd. 鼓 has a drum 壴 and a hand 支 holding the stick.
column6: Lǎoshī de huà gǔwǔ le dàjiā.
column7: The teacher's words encouraged everyone.
column9: To inspire, encourage, boost morale: 受到鼓舞, 鼓舞士氣, 令人鼓舞 "encouraging". The person is lifted up in spirit. 鼓 "drum" + 舞 "dance": drums and dancing lift a crowd. 鼓 has a drum 壴 and a hand 支 holding the stick.

column3: Husband of one's father's sister, an uncle by marriage: 我姑丈. Also written 姑父. The father's sister is 姑姑. 姑 has 女 "woman" and 古 for the sound (gǔ and gū are close); 丈 here means a man of the older generation (as in 丈夫 "husband").
column6: Wǒ gūzhàng zài yīyuàn gōngzuò.
column7: My uncle (my aunt's husband) works in a hospital.
column9: Husband of one's father's sister, an uncle by marriage: 我姑丈. Also written 姑父. The father's sister is 姑姑. 姑 has 女 "woman" and 古 for the sound (gǔ and gū are close); 丈 here means a man of the older generation (as in 丈夫 "husband").

column3: Might as well, would be better to, comparing two choices and saying the second wins: 还不如自己做, 还不如不去. It is used when something is pointless or worse than the alternative. 还 "even more" + 不如 "not as good as".
column4: 等这么久，还不如自己走路去。
column5: 等這麼久，還不如自己走路去。
column6: Děng zhème jiǔ, háibùrú zìjǐ zǒulù qù.
column7: Waiting this long, I might as well walk.
column9: Might as well, would be better to, comparing two choices and saying the second wins: 還不如自己做, 還不如不去. It is used when something is pointless or worse than the alternative. 還 "even more" + 不如 "not as good as".

column3: Harm, disadvantage, the opposite of 好处: 有害处, 对身体有害处, 没有什么害处. 害 "harm" + 处 "place, aspect", and 处 is read neutral here. Unlike 坏处, it says what damage something causes.
column4: 抽烟对身体有很多害处。
column5: 抽菸對身體有很多害處。
column6: Chōuyān duì shēntǐ yǒu hěn duō hàichu.
column7: Smoking does a lot of harm to the body.
column9: Harm, disadvantage, the opposite of 好處: 有害處, 對身體有害處, 沒有什麼害處. 害 "harm" + 處 "place, aspect", and 處 is read neutral here. Unlike 壞處, it says what damage something causes.

column3: Navy: 海军军官, 海军陆战队 "Marine Corps". 海 "sea" + 军 "army", with 陆军 "army" and 空军 "air force" as the other two. 军 is also the sound part in 挥, though 挥 (huī) no longer sounds like it.
column4: 他在海军工作了二十年。
column5: 他在海軍工作了二十年。
column6: Tā zài hǎijūn gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
column7: He has worked in the navy for twenty years.
column9: Navy: 海軍軍官, 海軍陸戰隊 "Marine Corps". 海 "sea" + 軍 "army", with 陸軍 "army" and 空軍 "air force" as the other two. 軍 is also the sound part in 揮, though 揮 (huī) no longer sounds like it.

column3: Overseas, abroad: 海外华人, 海外留学, 海外市场, 旅居海外. It means across the sea from where you are: anywhere abroad. 海 has 氵 "water" and 每, which still hints at the sound (hǎi, měi).
column6: Tā de jiārén dōu zài hǎiwài.
column7: His family are all overseas.
column9: Overseas, abroad: 海外華人, 海外留學, 海外市場, 旅居海外. It means across the sea from where you are: anywhere abroad. 海 has 氵 "water" and 每, which still hints at the sound (hǎi, měi).

column3: Strait, channel: 台湾海峡, 英吉利海峡. In Taiwan 海峡两岸 means the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, Taiwan and mainland China, a stock phrase in news and politics. 峡 has 山 "mountain" and 夹, a gap between two mountains (the same sound part as in 夹).
column4: 台湾海峡在台湾和大陆之间。
column5: 台灣海峽在台灣和大陸之間。
column6: Táiwān hǎixiá zài Táiwān hé dàlù zhījiān.
column7: The Taiwan Strait lies between Taiwan and the mainland.
column9: Strait, channel: 臺灣海峽, 英吉利海峽. In Taiwan 海峽兩岸 means the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, Taiwan and mainland China, a stock phrase in news and politics. 峽 has 山 "mountain" and 夾, a gap between two mountains (the same sound part as in 夾).

column3: To use up, consume, waste: 耗时 "time-consuming", 耗电 "power-hungry", 耗费, 耗掉 "burn through", 耗体力. It is something that drains a resource. The old form 秏 had 禾; today's 耗 has 耒 "plow" with 毛 as the (loose) sound.
column6: Zhège ruǎntǐ hěn hào diàn.
column7: This software uses a lot of battery.
column9: To use up, consume, waste: 耗時 "time-consuming", 耗電 "power-hungry", 耗費, 耗掉 "burn through", 耗體力. It is something that drains a resource. The old form 秏 had 禾; today's 耗 has 耒 "plow" with 毛 as the (loose) sound.

column3: Hospitable, fond of having guests: 热情好客, 好客的主人. Note the reading: 好 is hào "to like", so the word means "likes guests", not "good guest". 客 shows a roof 宀 with the person under it, and 各 gives the sound.
column6: Tāmen yījiārén dōu hěn hàokè.
column7: His whole family is very hospitable.
column9: Hospitable, fond of having guests: 熱情好客, 好客的主人. Note the reading: 好 is hào "to like", so the word means "likes guests", not "good guest". 客 shows a roof 宀 with the person under it, and 各 gives the sound.

column3: Not at all, completely without, before a noun and mainly in writing: 毫无疑问 "without doubt", 毫无意义, 毫无根据 "baseless", 毫无办法. 毫 is a hair's breadth (it contains 毛 "hair"), so 毫无 is "not even a hair of". For spoken use, 一点也没有.
column6: Zhège juédìng háowú dàolǐ.
column7: This decision makes no sense at all.
column9: Not at all, completely without, before a noun and mainly in writing: 毫無疑問 "without doubt", 毫無意義, 毫無根據 "baseless", 毫無辦法. 毫 is a hair's breadth (it contains 毛 "hair"), so 毫無 is "not even a hair of". For spoken use, 一點也沒有.

column3: Luckily, fortunately, pointing to what saved the situation: 好在我带了伞, 好在没有人受伤. It comes before the clause naming the lucky fact. 好 "good" + 在 "being there": a good thing that ...
column6: Hǎozài wǒ dài le sǎn.
column7: Luckily I brought an umbrella.
column9: Luckily, fortunately, pointing to what saved the situation: 好在我帶了傘, 好在沒有人受傷. It comes before the clause naming the lucky fact. 好 "good" + 在 "being there": a good thing that ...

column3: Why bother, there's no need, a rhetorical question: 何必生气, 何必这么麻烦? It says the effort or the feeling is unnecessary. 何 "why" is literary and 必 "must": "why must you".
column4: 事情这么小，你何必生气？
column5: 事情這麼小，你何必生氣？
column6: Shìqing zhème xiǎo, nǐ hébì shēngqì?
column7: It's such a small matter, why get angry?
column9: Why bother, there's no need, a rhetorical question: 何必生氣, 何必這麼麻煩? It says the effort or the feeling is unnecessary. 何 "why" is literary and 必 "must": "why must you".

column3: Cannot get along, of people whose personalities clash: 我跟他合不来, 性格合不来. The opposite is 合得来. The pattern 合不来 is the "can't" form of 合来, "fit together".
column4: 我跟他的性格不同，合不来。
column5: 我跟他的性格不同，合不來。
column6: Wǒ gēn tā de xìnggé bùtóng, hébùlái.
column7: His personality differs from mine, and we don't get along.
column9: Cannot get along, of people whose personalities clash: 我跟他合不來, 性格合不來. The opposite is 合得來. The pattern 合不來 is the "can't" form of 合來, "fit together".

column3: To get along well, be compatible: 我们很合得来, 跟同事合得来. It is the positive partner of 合不来. It is for personality fit, not for similar likes. The 得 is neutral, as in other "can" forms.
column6: Wǒmen liǎ hěn hédelái.
column7: We two get along very well.
column9: To get along well, be compatible: 我們很合得來, 跟同事合得來. It is the positive partner of 合不來. It is for personality fit, not for similar likes. The 得 is neutral, as in other "can" forms.

column3: To make up, be reconciled: 吵架后和好, 和好如初 "be as good as before". It is used for friends, couples or families after a quarrel. 和 here is hé "peace, harmony", not hàn or huò.
column4: 他们吵架以后很快就和好了。
column5: 他們吵架以後很快就和好了。
column6: Tāmen chǎojià yǐhòu hěn kuài jiù héhǎo le.
column7: After their quarrel they soon made up.
column9: To make up, be reconciled: 吵架後和好, 和好如初 "be as good as before". It is used for friends, couples or families after a quarrel. 和 here is hé "peace, harmony", not hàn or huò.

column3: To conform to, meet a standard, rule or expectation: 合乎标准, 合乎规定, 合乎逻辑 "logical", 合乎要求. It is formal, written style. 合 "match" + 乎, a literary particle that works like 于 here.
column6: Zhège chǎnpǐn héhū biāozhǔn.
column7: This product meets the standard.
column9: To conform to, meet a standard, rule or expectation: 合乎標準, 合乎規定, 合乎邏輯 "logical", 合乎要求. It is formal, written style. 合 "match" + 乎, a literary particle that works like 於 here.

column3: Hey!, to get someone's attention or to greet: 嘿, 你在这里做什么? Doubled, 嘿嘿 is a sly laugh. It is spoken and casual. 口 shows the mouth, and 黑 gives the sound (hēi, the same).
column6: Hēi, nǐ zài zhèlǐ zuò shénme?
column7: Hey, what are you doing here?
column9: Hey!, to get someone's attention or to greet: 嘿, 你在這裡做什麼? Doubled, 嘿嘿 is a sly laugh. It is spoken and casual. 口 shows the mouth, and 黑 gives the sound (hēi, the same).

column3: Night, the dark of night, used with some feeling: 在黑夜里, 黑夜过去，黎明到来. The plain word for night is 晚上 or 夜晚. 黑 shows a face blackened by soot, with 灬 "fire" under it; 夜 is "night".
column6: Tā yī ge rén zǒu zài hēiyè lǐ.
column7: He walks alone in the dark of night.
column9: Night, the dark of night, used with some feeling: 在黑夜裡, 黑夜過去，黎明到來. The plain word for night is 晚上 or 夜晚. 黑 shows a face blackened by soot, with 灬 "fire" under it; 夜 is "night".

column3: Let alone, moreover: A都…，何况B: 大人都做不到，何况小孩 "even adults can't, let alone children". The second case is clearer than the first. 况 has 冫, and its sound part 兄 is not like kuàng any more.
column4: 大人都做不到，何况小孩。
column5: 大人都做不到，何況小孩。
column6: Dàrén dōu zuòbùdào, hékuàng xiǎohái.
column7: Even adults can't do it, let alone children.
column9: Let alone, moreover: A都…，何況B: 大人都做不到，何況小孩 "even adults can't, let alone children". The second case is clearer than the first. 況 has 氵 "water", and its sound part 兄 is not like kuàng any more.

column3: Rivers, as a group or in geography: 河流污染, 河流的上游, 台湾的河流. 河流 speaks of rivers in general, where 河 or 溪 names a single one. 河 has 氵 "water" and 可 for the sound (hé, kě); 流 adds 㐬 for the sound.
column6: Táiwān de héliú dàduō hěn duǎn.
column7: Most of Taiwan's rivers are short.
column9: Rivers, as a group or in geography: 河流污染, 河流的上游, 臺灣的河流. 河流 speaks of rivers in general, where 河 or 溪 names a single one. 河 has 氵 "water" and 可 for the sound (hé, kě); 流 adds 㐬 for the sound.

column3: Horizontal, across, sideways: 横线, 横过马路 "cross the road", 把桌子横着放. Also the horizontal stroke 一 in a character. The opposite is 直 or 竖. In words like 蛮横 "overbearing" it is read hèng. 木 "wood" is the meaning (a beam) and 黄 gives a sound that is close.
column6: Wǒ bǎ zhuōzi héng zhe fàng.
column7: I put the table down sideways.
column9: Horizontal, across, sideways: 橫線, 橫過馬路 "cross the road", 把桌子橫著放. Also the horizontal stroke 一 in a character. The opposite is 直 or 豎. In words like 蠻橫 "overbearing" it is read hèng. 木 "wood" is the meaning (a beam) and 黃 gives a sound that is close.

column3: Trace, mark, vestige: 留下痕迹, 岁月的痕迹, 没有留下任何痕迹. 痕 has 疒 "sickness", like a mark left on the skin, and 艮; 迹 has 辶 and 亦.
column6: Qiáng shàng liúxià le shuǐ de hénjì.
column7: The water left marks on the wall.
column9: Trace, mark, vestige: 留下痕跡, 歲月的痕跡, 沒有留下任何痕跡. 痕 has 疒 "sickness", like a mark left on the skin, and 艮; 跡 has 足 "foot", a footprint. Both parts describe something left behind.

column3: Friendly, amiable, polite in manner: 对人和气, 和和气气, 和气生财 "friendliness brings wealth". It describes a pleasant, mild attitude. The second syllable is neutral.
column6: Lǎobǎn duì kèrén hěn héqi.
column7: The boss is very friendly to customers.
column9: Friendly, amiable, polite in manner: 對人和氣, 和和氣氣, 和氣生財 "friendliness brings wealth". It describes a pleasant, mild attitude. The second syllable is neutral.

column3: Worth the price, a good deal: 买大包装比较合算, 这样合算吗? 划算 means the same and is more common. It is about whether money is well spent. 算 has 竹 "bamboo" on top, since counting rods were bamboo, and a figure with hands below.
column6: Mǎi dà bāozhuāng bǐjiào hésuàn.
column7: It's a better deal to buy the large pack.
column9: Worth the price, a good deal: 買大包裝比較合算, 這樣合算嗎? 划算 means the same and is more common. It is about whether money is well spent. 算 has 竹 "bamboo" on top, since counting rods were bamboo, and a figure with hands below.

column3: Contract, agreement: 签合约, 合约到期, 租屋合约 "rental contract", 手机合约. In Taiwan 合约 is the usual word, 合同 being the mainland one. 合 "fit together" + 约 "bind, appoint"; 约 has 纟 "thread" for something that binds.
column6: Wǒmen míngtiān yào qiān héyuē.
column7: We will sign the contract tomorrow.
column9: Contract, agreement: 簽合約, 合約到期, 租屋合約 "rental contract", 手機合約. In Taiwan 合約 is the usual word, 合同 being the mainland one. 合 "fit together" + 約 "bind, appoint"; 約 has 糹 "thread" for something that binds.

column3: Monkey: 一只猴子, 猴子爬树, and the saying 猴子捞月. 猴 has 犭 "animal" and 侯 for the sound (hóu, the same). 子 is a neutral suffix.
column4: 动物园里的猴子很可爱。
column5: 動物園裡的猴子很可愛。
column6: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de hóuzi hěn kě'ài.
column7: The monkeys in the zoo are cute.
column9: Monkey: 一隻猴子, 猴子爬樹, and the saying 猴子撈月. 猴 has 犭 "animal" and 侯 for the sound (hóu, the same). 子 is a neutral suffix.

column3: Descendants, later generations: 子孙后代, 留给后代, 为后代着想. It looks at the family or humanity from the point of view of the future.
column4: 我们要为后代保护环境。
column5: 我們要為後代保護環境。
column6: Wǒmen yào wèi hòudài bǎohù huánjìng.
column7: We must protect the environment for later generations.
column9: Descendants, later generations: 子孫後代, 留給後代, 為後代著想. It looks at the family or humanity from the point of view of the future. 後 shows a step 彳 and a foot 夂 tied by thread 幺, a foot that lags behind.

column3: The rear, behind: 车子后方, 后方来车 "traffic from behind", a common road warning. It also means the area behind the front line in war. It is more formal and technical than 后面.
column6: Qǐng zhùyì hòufāng lái chē.
column7: Watch out for traffic from behind.
column9: The rear, behind: 車子後方, 後方來車 "traffic from behind", a common road warning. It also means the area behind the front line in war. It is more formal and technical than 後面.

column3: Throat: 喉咙痛 "sore throat", 喉咙发炎, 清喉咙 "clear one's throat". Both characters have 口 "mouth" for the meaning; 喉 is sounded by 侯 (hóu, the same) and 咙 by 龙 (lóng, the same).
column6: Wǒ hóulóng hěn tòng.
column7: My throat is very sore.
column9: Throat: 喉嚨痛 "sore throat", 喉嚨發炎, 清喉嚨 "clear one's throat". Both characters have 口 "mouth" for the meaning; 喉 is sounded by 侯 (hóu, the same) and 嚨 by 龍 (lóng, the same).

column3: Throat, larynx, mostly in compounds: 喉咙, 喉结 "Adam's apple", 咽喉 "throat", 喉科 "ear-nose-throat". 口 "mouth" is the meaning part and 侯 gives the sound (hóu, the same).
column6: Tā de hóujié hěn míngxiǎn.
column7: His Adam's apple is very noticeable.
column9: Throat, larynx, mostly in compounds: 喉嚨, 喉結 "Adam's apple", 咽喉 "throat", 喉科 "ear-nose-throat". 口 "mouth" is the meaning part and 侯 gives the sound (hóu, the same).

column3: To move back, retreat: 向后退, 请后退, 车子慢慢后退. Said to a crowd as an instruction, and also for armies and for falling behind in a competition. 退 has 辶 "walk" and 艮, and the old form was about leaving the table after a meal.
column6: Chēzi mànmàn hòutuì.
column7: The car slowly backs up.
column9: To move back, retreat: 向後退, 請後退, 車子慢慢後退. Said to a crowd as an instruction, and also for armies and for falling behind in a competition. 退 has 辶 "walk" and 艮, and the old form was about leaving the table after a meal.

column3: Backyard, behind a house: 后院种菜, and in figurative speech 后院起火 "trouble at home". 院 has 阝 "mound, place" and 完 for the sound (yuàn, wán). It is the opposite of 前院.
column4: 我家的后院种了很多花。
column5: 我家的後院種了很多花。
column6: Wǒ jiā de hòuyuàn zhòng le hěn duō huā.
column7: We have planted many flowers in our backyard.
column9: Backyard, behind a house: 後院種菜, and in figurative speech 後院起火 "trouble at home". 院 has 阝 "mound, place" and 完 for the sound (yuàn, wán). It is the opposite of 前院.

column3: To breathe out; to call: 呼吸 "breathe", 呼叫 "call out", 呼喊 "shout", 招呼, 打招呼 "greet", 称呼 "address as". It is mostly in compounds. 口 "mouth" is the meaning and 乎 the sound (hū, the same). Its opposite is 吸 "breathe in".
column6: Tā qīngqīng hū chū yī kǒu qì.
column7: She breathed out softly.
column9: To breathe out; to call: 呼吸 "breathe", 呼叫 "call out", 呼喊 "shout", 招呼, 打招呼 "greet", 稱呼 "address as". It is mostly in compounds. 口 "mouth" is the meaning and 乎 the sound (hū, the same). Its opposite is 吸 "breathe in".

column3: The word is "beard", whiskers: 胡子, 胡须, 刮胡子 "to shave". 胡 has ⺼ and 古 for the sound. 胡子 is the spoken word and 胡须 sounds more written.
column6: Bàba měi tiān zǎoshang guā húzi.
column7: Dad shaves every morning.
column9: The word is "beard", whiskers: 鬍子, 鬍鬚, 刮鬍子 "to shave". 鬍 has 髟 "long hair" with 胡 for the sound. 鬍子 is the spoken word and 鬍鬚 sounds more written. 鬍 comes from the old sense of 胡, the dewlap, what hangs down from the chin.

column3: Flowers and plants, the greenery of a garden or balcony: 种花草, 照顾花草, 花草树木. It names plants grown for looks. 花 has 艹 "plant" with 化 for the sound (huā, huà are close), and 草 has 艹 and 早, whose sound is also close (cǎo, zǎo).
column6: Yángtái shàng bǎimǎn le huācǎo.
column7: The balcony is full of flowers and plants.
column9: Flowers and plants, the greenery of a garden or balcony: 種花草, 照顧花草, 花草樹木. It names plants grown for looks. 花 has 艹 "plant" with 化 for the sound (huā, huà are close), and 草 has 艹 and 早, whose sound is also close (cǎo, zǎo).

column3: Cost, expense, and the verb "to spend" (money, time, effort): 旅行的花费, 花费很多时间, 花费不少. It is used for the total spent on something. 费 has 贝 "shell", the old money, with 弗 for the sound.
column6: Zhè cì lǚxíng de huāfèi bù shǎo.
column7: This trip cost quite a lot.
column9: Cost, expense, and the verb "to spend" (money, time, effort): 旅行的花費, 花費很多時間, 花費不少. It is used for the total spent on something. 費 has 貝 "shell", the old money, with 弗 for the sound.

column3: Scoundrel, literally "bad egg": 大坏蛋, 坏蛋被抓住了. It is mild, common with children and in stories and films. 坏 has 土 "earth" for something that collapses, and 蛋 has 虫 "insect" for the creature and 延 for the sound.
column4: 电影里的坏蛋被抓住了。
column5: 電影裡的壞蛋被抓住了。
column6: Diànyǐng lǐ de huàidàn bèi zhuāzhù le.
column7: The villain in the film was caught.
column9: Scoundrel, literally "bad egg": 大壞蛋, 壞蛋被抓住了. It is mild, common with children and in stories and films. 壞 has 土 "earth" for something that collapses, and 蛋 has 虫 "insect" for the creature and 延 for the sound.

column3: Pregnant, to become pregnant: 她怀孕了, 怀孕三个月, 孕妇 "pregnant woman". It is neutral and polite. 怀 has 忄 "heart" and means to carry in the bosom; 孕 is a picture of a woman with a child inside.
column6: Tā huáiyùn sān ge yuè le.
column7: She is three months pregnant.
column9: Pregnant, to become pregnant: 她懷孕了, 懷孕三個月, 孕婦 "pregnant woman". It is neutral and polite. 懷 has 忄 "heart" and means to carry in the bosom; 孕 is a picture of a woman with a child inside.

column3: Emperor: 中国的皇帝, 秦始皇 "the first emperor", 皇帝的新衣 "the emperor's new clothes". 皇 and 帝 each mean "sovereign" alone, and 皇帝 joins them. 皇 shows a crown 白 above 王 "king".
column4: 他是中国最后一个皇帝。
column5: 他是中國最後一個皇帝。
column6: Tā shì Zhōngguó zuìhòu yī ge huángdì.
column7: He was China's last emperor.
column9: Emperor: 中國的皇帝, 秦始皇 "the first emperor", 皇帝的新衣 "the emperor's new clothes". 皇 and 帝 each mean "sovereign" alone, and 皇帝 joins them. 皇 shows a crown 白 above 王 "king".

column3: Soybean, the dry yellow bean from which soy milk, tofu and soy sauce are made: 黄豆浆, 黄豆粉. The green young pods eaten as a snack are 毛豆. 豆 began as a picture of a serving dish on a stand and was later used for beans.
column6: Dòujiāng shì yòng huángdòu zuò de.
column7: Soy milk is made from soybeans.
column9: Soybean, the dry yellow bean from which soy milk, tofu and soy sauce are made: 黃豆漿, 黃豆粉. The green young pods eaten as a snack are 毛豆. 豆 began as a picture of a serving dish on a stand and was later used for beans.

column3: Dusk, twilight: 黄昏的海边, 黄昏时分, 黄昏市场 "evening market". It has a poetic feel; the everyday words are 傍晚 or 晚上. 昏 shows the sun 日 going down under 氏; the same character means "dim" and "faint" in 昏倒 and 昏迷.
column4: 黄昏的时候，天空变成了橘红色。
column5: 黃昏的時候，天空變成了橘紅色。
column6: Huánghūn de shíhou, tiānkōng biànchéng le júhóngsè.
column7: At dusk the sky turns orange.
column9: Dusk, twilight: 黃昏的海邊, 黃昏時分, 黃昏市場 "evening market". It has a poetic feel; the everyday words are 傍晚 or 晚上. 昏 shows the sun 日 going down under 氏; the same character means "dim" and "faint" in 昏倒 and 昏迷.

column3: To ease, relax tension or a situation: 缓和气氛, 缓和紧张, 局势缓和. Also an adjective, "mild, gentle". It is about making something less sharp. 缓 has 纟 "thread" and 爰; 和 here is hé, not hè.
column4: 他开了个玩笑，缓和了气氛。
column5: 他開了個玩笑，緩和了氣氛。
column6: Tā kāi le ge wánxiào, huǎnhé le qìfēn.
column7: He made a joke and eased the mood.
column9: To ease, relax tension or a situation: 緩和氣氛, 緩和緊張, 局勢緩和. Also an adjective, "mild, gentle". It is about making something less sharp. 緩 has 糹 "thread" and 爰; 和 here is hé, not hè.

column3: To cheer, hail: 欢呼声, 为他欢呼, 欢呼起来. It is a cry of joy from a crowd. 欢 has 欠 "breath, yawn" and 又. 呼 is "to call out".
column6: Guānzhòng wèi xuǎnshǒu huānhū.
column7: The audience cheered for the athlete.
column9: To cheer, hail: 歡呼聲, 為他歡呼, 歡呼起來. It is a cry of joy from a crowd. 歡 has 欠 "breath, yawn" and 雚 for the sound; 雚 is also in 觀 and 罐 (guān, guàn). 呼 is "to call out".

column3: Slow, formal and descriptive: 速度缓慢, 动作缓慢, 发展缓慢. 缓 "gentle" + 慢 "slow". 慢 has 忄 "heart" and 曼; in speech use plain 慢.
column6: Héshuǐ liú de hěn huǎnmàn.
column7: The river flows very slowly.
column9: Slow, formal and descriptive: 速度緩慢, 動作緩慢, 發展緩慢. 緩 "gentle" + 慢 "slow". 慢 has 忄 "heart" and 曼; in speech use plain 慢.

column3: Happy, delighted: 满心欢喜, 欢欢喜喜, 皆大欢喜 "everyone is happy". It is also a verb, "to like", in some regions. 喜 shows a drum 壴 above a mouth 口, singing and drumming.
column4: 他满心欢喜地接过礼物。
column5: 他滿心歡喜地接過禮物。
column6: Tā mǎnxīn huānxǐ de jiēguò lǐwù.
column7: He took the gift, full of joy.
column9: Happy, delighted: 滿心歡喜, 歡歡喜喜, 皆大歡喜 "everyone is happy". It is also a verb, "to like", in some regions. 喜 shows a drum 壴 above a mouth 口, singing and drumming.

column3: To fantasize; a fantasy: 不要幻想, 幻想成真, 沉迷于幻想. The ideas are unrealistic or hopeful. 幻 "illusion" + 想 "think". 想 has 心 "heart" and 相 for the sound (xiǎng, xiāng).
column4: 他常常幻想自己是超人。
column5: 他常常幻想自己是超人。
column6: Tā chángcháng huànxiǎng zìjǐ shì chāorén.
column7: He often fantasizes that he is Superman.
column9: To fantasize; a fantasy: 不要幻想, 幻想成真, 沉迷於幻想. The ideas are unrealistic or hopeful. 幻 "illusion" + 想 "think". 想 has 心 "heart" and 相 for the sound (xiǎng, xiāng).

column3: Flowerpot: 一个花盆, 换花盆, 花盆里的土. 盆 shows a dish 皿 under 分, whose sound is close (pén, fēn). 盆 alone is a basin, as in 脸盆 and 盆栽 "potted plant".
column4: 他在花盆里种了一棵小树。
column5: 他在花盆裡種了一棵小樹。
column6: Tā zài huāpén lǐ zhòng le yī kē xiǎoshù.
column7: He planted a small tree in a flowerpot.
column9: Flowerpot: 一個花盆, 換花盆, 花盆裡的土. 盆 shows a dish 皿 under 分, whose sound is close (pén, fēn). 盆 alone is a basin, as in 臉盆 and 盆栽 "potted plant".

column3: Vase: 插花的花瓶, 一个花瓶. Figuratively, for a woman or a man valued only for looks: 他只是个花瓶. 瓶 has 瓦 "earthenware", for something made of clay, and 并 for the sound (píng, bìng).
column4: 桌上有一个漂亮的花瓶。
column5: 桌上有一個漂亮的花瓶。
column6: Zhuō shàng yǒu yī ge piàoliang de huāpíng.
column7: There is a pretty vase on the table.
column9: Vase: 插花的花瓶, 一個花瓶. Figuratively, for a woman or a man valued only for looks: 他只是個花瓶. 瓶 has 瓦 "earthenware", for something made of clay, and 并 for the sound (píng, bìng).

column3: Overseas Chinese, strictly a Chinese person who lives abroad but keeps Chinese nationality; 华人 is a person of Chinese origin of any nationality. In Taiwan, 华侨 and 侨生 (an overseas Chinese student studying in Taiwan) are common. 华 was once the older form of 花 "flower", then "splendid", hence "Chinese". 侨 has 亻 "person" with 乔 for the sound.
column6: Tā shì zhù zài Tàiguó de huáqiáo.
column7: He is an overseas Chinese living in Thailand.
